chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Breast-feeding is for twenty-one months, so whatever is deficient [from this period], it is an injustice upon the child.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed duration for breast-feeding in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes twenty-one months as the complete duration of breast-feeding, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) noting that any reduction constitutes 'injustice' (jawr) to the child, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maximizing maternal and infant welfare. While the Quranic verse 2:233 sets a two-year baseline, this narration clarifies the jurisprudential standard for the 'complete' period, distinguishing between the minimum obligation and the ideal practice for nurturing. This interpretation underscores the holistic view of child-rearing in Shia fiqh, where physical nourishment is linked to spiritual and emotional justice.
